name: Boogie Down Productions
hook: Answered a record they heard as writing the Bronx out of hip-hop's own origin story, and won the argument so completely it ended the other side's career momentum.
blurb: KRS-One and DJ Scott La Rock formed Boogie Down Productions in the South Bronx. They heard MC Shan's 'The Bridge' as a claim that hip-hop began in Queensbridge, and answered first with 'South Bronx' and then 'The Bridge Is Over' (1986 and 1987), insisting the Bronx came first and starting the Bridge Wars. Their side is widely treated as hip-hop's first well-documented case of a diss record settling an argument with the public, and 'The Bridge Is Over' is still commonly ranked among the most effective answer records. Scott La Rock was shot and killed in the Bronx in August 1987, while trying to calm down an unrelated dispute involving a group member, months after their first album 'Criminal Minded' came out and only a year into their partnership. KRS-One kept the group going, turned toward openly political songs, and later had a long solo career.
